paragraphs: An alert shows a short, sentiment-coded message inline on the page, with an optional action and close button.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Alerts surface feedback inline on the page. Each sentiment has its own colors and icon. The action and close buttons are real Button instances, and the icon is a real Icon instance.

sections.heading: Sentiments
paragraphs: Neutral, Info, Success, Warning and Danger — each maps to its own background, border, text and icon tokens and its own status icon.

sections.heading: Configurations
paragraphs: Default, With Action, With Close, and With Action + Close.

sections.heading: Anatomy
paragraphs: •   ① Container — carries the sentiment background, border, padding and radius.
•   ② Leading icon — the sentiment's status icon (an Icon instance).
•   ⑤ Action button — a Button instance (Ghost, Sm).
•   ⑥ Close button — a Button instance with its label hidden (icon only).

sections.heading: Sizes
paragraphs: Spacing comes from the component.alert.density variable collection, with Compact, Comfortable and Spacious modes.
Use a Ghost, Sm Button for the action — matching the alert's compact footprint.
Don't use a large primary button — it overpowers the alert.

sections.heading: Overflow content
paragraphs: Text wraps. The skill defines a truncate-text option (ellipsis, with a tooltip for the full text in code); it isn't exposed as a Figma property yet.

sections.heading: States
paragraphs: The alert itself has no interactive states — sentiment changes swap its background, border, icon and text tokens. The action and close buttons inherit Default, Hover, Pressed, Focused and Disabled from Button.

sections.heading: Interactions
paragraphs: •   Close — dismisses the alert, collapsing it out of the layout.
•   Action — runs the alert's action; while it's running, the action button shows its loading state.
Moves focus to the action button, then the close button
Button behavior is inherited from the Button component.

sections.heading: Related
paragraphs: •   Button — used for the action and close controls.
•   Dialog — for urgent messages that must interrupt the page; alerts stay inline.

sections.heading: Color
paragraphs: Each sentiment aliases its own component.alert tokens. Swatches are bound to the live tokens.
Headline and supporting text share one label token per sentiment. Button colors belong to the Button component.

sections.heading: Typography
paragraphs: Text isn't bound to typography tokens yet (raw values).

sections.heading: Variants & states
paragraphs: 40 variants: Sentiment (5) × Size (2) × State (4). Grid shows Sentiment × State at Size=Md.

sections.heading: Icons
paragraphs: Neutral and Info use Icon/status/info, Success uses Icon/status/success, Warning uses Icon/status/warning and Danger uses Icon/status/error — 16px at Sm, 20px at Md.
An alert shows a short, sentiment-coded message inline on the page, with an optional action and close button.

sections.heading: What the design system provides
paragraphs: •   Each sentiment pairs its color with a distinct status icon, so meaning doesn't rely on color alone.
•   Action and close controls are real Buttons, with Button's focus and disabled states.

sections.heading: Development considerations
paragraphs: •   Use role="alert" for assertive, urgent messages and role="status" for polite ones.
•   The close button is icon-only — give it an accessible name (e.g. "Dismiss").
•   Show loading on the action with the Button's is-loading state, not a separate spinner.
•   When text is truncated, provide the full text in a tooltip.

sections.heading: Keyboard interactions
paragraphs: Moves focus to the action button, then the close button

sections.heading: Design recommendations
paragraphs: Automated contrast check — WCAG 2.x relative luminance (sRGB), text and icon against the alert background, border against the page surface, for every theme combination. Minimums: 4.5:1 for text (12–13px), 3:1 for the icon and border. Note: project-a / light is measured against the current surface/bg/default, which resolves to blue because of the gray/50 token.
